headlines.why_it_matters: The overnight fade eased a touch from the 7:30 AM ET lows (S&P -0.69%, Nasdaq -1.46%), but the open still starts in the red with tech leading down.

headlines.headline: Nvidia faces fresh analyst pressure: UBS cut its price target to $240 from $300, citing potential export curbs that could depress 2028 revenue expectations, with other major banks also cutting targets (TradingKey). NVDA traded between -2.3% and -3.9% premarket (~$156.59-158.96) after falling ~13% last week to $162.85. Earnings are Tue Nov 17 after the close (consensus ~$108.9B revenue, ~$2.47 EPS; options imply a ~7% move).
headlines.why_it_matters: The target cuts add a fundamental, numbers-based headwind on top of the governance overhang — the stock is being repriced on earnings power, not just on who runs the company.

headlines.headline: The Huang-return debate splits openly: analyst Dan Ives called any talk of Jensen Huang returning 'ridiculous' and 'gone for good,' floating Tim Cook and Arm's Rene Haas as good fits for the permanent CEO job. That counters the weekend FT report that Huang has discussed a return with confidants, the 'Stand with Jensen' petition past 171,000 signatures, and Bessent's push for an outside CEO and a 'dramatic shakeup.' Nvidia says it is selecting a search firm and has not formally engaged candidates; Colette Kress remains interim CEO.
headlines.why_it_matters: Two credible camps are now arguing in public with no board decision — the return story is sentiment, not a catalyst, and the split keeps the leadership discount in the stock into earnings.

headlines.headline: Micron adds two fresh headaches: a fatal construction accident at its Central Taiwan Science Park Houli site (an excavator overturned; the operator did not survive) led Micron to voluntarily suspend construction in the affected area, and a judge refused to toss the DRAM cartel suit against Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron. That sits on top of the ongoing Taoyuan labor dispute that has largely paused construction of the $3-4.5B Fab 11E. MU is down ~5-6% premarket; Asia set the tone overnight with Taiwan's Taiex -6.03% and TSMC -5.74%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The accident is a real but small construction-site event, not a production outage — yet it compounds the memory-supply anxiety already pressuring the whole chip complex ahead of Nvidia's print.

headlines.why_it_matters: Apple and Microsoft remain the only green megacaps — the rotation is still narrowing to names without a fresh overhang, while crypto-linked names stay under pressure.
